note: Budget approval; names ANSIE as the state's information-systems agency but states no systems it runs for ministries.
Capacity-building exchange visit; names ANSIE's director-general as a delegate but states no systems run or built by staff.

facts.fact: eGA experts supported ANSIE, the government ICT coordination unit, in setting up a national data exchange layer and drafted the national interoperability framework for it, in a Government of Djibouti-funded project (EUR 52,800) running May 2022 to April 2023; the page is undated, so the date is the proxy publication month.

note: X-Road was implemented by contractors (eGA with Roksnet, Gofore, UpMind) for ANSIE, the beneficiary; the page does not state ANSIE staff run it, and training courses are not facts.
Digital skills centres for citizens (E-SKILLS programme); no government system run or built by government staff.
Training course for officials (Oracle University, DCO, INAP); training is not a fact and no system is named.
Projected jobs and training options for a planned private AI compute build; no government staff running or building systems.
ANSIE gives technical support to the e-Cabinet platform, but the article does not say it builds or runs systems for ministries.

facts.fact: The Council of Ministers examined a draft decree pricing the services ANSIE provides under agreement to public and parapublic institutions, including hosting, dedicated applications, technical assistance and network security support, and says ANSIE has offered such services since its creation.

systems.country_label: Agence Nationale des Systemes d'Information de l'Etat

note: No government technical staff or IT body is described.
The state information systems agency is named only as holding a conference; no staff running systems is stated.
ANSIE's director general is named as attending; no statement on who runs or builds government systems.

facts.fact: The Council of Ministers communique of 14 January 2025 approves ANSIE's 2025 budget of 556.7 million FDJ, covering its work for administrations on the E-JO and E-BALO platforms, archive digitisation, a human-resources solution and support to the social registry.

note: Only stated aims for local firms and skills; no staffing, agency or system built stated.
Works are given to Djibouti Telecom and ANSIE only supervises; no system built or run by government staff stated.

facts.fact: ADI reports that Djibouti's customs directorate DGDDI built its own data centre in 2010 after the DP World-run Mirsal system, adopted SydoniaWorld in 2012 on it, and invested in training its teams to use it.
